subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser routes adopt the proposed fail-safe public contract—return the stale acted-on target and require a fresh explicit selection whenever continuity is not proven—or must extension relay provide a stable public target handle before this route-safety change lands?
rationale: The branch removes an unsafe heuristic, but choosing between fail-safe re-selection and stable relay continuity changes the supported recovery behavior for existing browser clients and cannot be resolved from route code alone.

options.title: Accept explicit re-selection fallback
options.body: Approve stale acted-on target IDs as the intentional recovery contract, then require paired extension-relay proof that clients fail safely and can reselect.

options.title: Require relay-owned stable continuity first
options.body: Keep this PR open until the relay bridge exposes a stable public handle across renderer detach/reattach and the route outcome is proven against that contract.

options.title: Narrow to managed Playwright and MCP
options.body: Split extension-relay behavior from this PR if maintainers want to land the independently proven managed Playwright and Chrome MCP safety changes first.

recommendation.title: Accept explicit re-selection fallback
recommendation.body: Approve stale acted-on target IDs as the intentional recovery contract, then require paired extension-relay proof that clients fail safely and can reselect.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical issue and the PR discussion both identify this as a browser identity-contract choice requiring their direction.
